sources.title: qwen-omni-turbo model information (Japanese documentation)
sources.evidence: Official model page, updated October 1, 2026, lists the exact stable API ID, equivalence to the March 26, 2025 snapshot, 32,768-token context (30,720 input plus 2,048 output), four input modalities, text/audio output, and unsupported function calling in Beijing and Singapore. English counterpart redirected to the general models page. Reopened October 27, 2026: this former model-specific page now redirects to the general Japanese models overview; the original observations above are retained as historical evidence.

sources.title: Model lifecycle and updates
sources.evidence: China (Beijing) release table explicitly lists qwen-omni-turbo and qwen-omni-turbo-latest on February 14, 2025. It separately lists the January 19 snapshot on March 17 and the March 26 snapshot on March 27; the international API release is July 18, 2025. Reopened October 27, 2026: the lifecycle table still lists the March 26 Qwen2.5-Omni-7B release separately from the March 27 Turbo snapshot release and does not publish a Turbo parameter count.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Omni official repository README
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The current official README presents qwen-omni-turbo as API access to Qwen2.5-Omni and includes both 7B and later 3B open releases. The launch-day README and announcement, added below, resolve the historical nominal-size relationship without requiring identical hosted and downloadable tensors.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio model pricing
sources.evidence: Indexed official pricing table (retrieved in web search) labels qwen-omni-turbo and its snapshots Non-Thinking mode, and the stable alias equivalent to the March 26 snapshot. The newer directly opened page no longer included these older rows; this evidence is the retained indexed primary page, not a live API test.

sources.title: Qwen2.5 Omni launch announcement, March 26, 2025 revision
sources.evidence: Read the original developer blog through its immutable GitHub source after the live blog redirected. The opening introduces Qwen2.5-Omni, explicitly names Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, and then says the model is available on Hugging Face, ModelScope, DashScope and GitHub. It describes the Thinker-Talker architecture. This supplies the named nominal 7B model behind the launch API relationship; the later 3B release does not negate that dated statement.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Omni launch-day README, March 26, 2025
sources.evidence: Read the March 26 developer commit, located using GitHub commit history. Its API Inference section explicitly offers interaction with Qwen2.5-Omni and calls model="qwen-omni-turbo"; its released checkpoint and evaluation labels are Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. Combined with the launch announcement, this supports inherited nominal 7B size. No pruning, distillation, expert expansion or added modality relative to the announced multimodal model is described. API voice choices differ, so no exact tensor identity is claimed.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Omni Technical Report, original version
sources.evidence: Freshly read the original report. Section 5.1.1 compares the released model with similarly sized 7B models, and Table 1 names Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. The architecture includes Thinker, Talker, vision/audio encoders and a speech decoder. It does not separately publish per-token active parameters or a parameter total for all these components; 7B is retained as the developer nominal model designation.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-Omni-7B official configuration
sources.evidence: Read only the small official config, without weights. It specifies dense Thinker text and Talker transformer configurations, vision/audio encoders and token2wav modules, with no routed-expert configuration. This supports the dense classification inherited from the explicitly named launch model; it is not an exact parameter census or independent claim about Turbo deployment tensors.

sources.title: Alibaba Cloud Omni-modal overview, legacy model list
sources.evidence: Freshly opened the current official overview. It lists qwen2.5-omni-7b and qwen-omni-turbo with its snapshots as separate legacy API IDs, without publishing total or active Turbo counts or describing a changed architecture. English and Chinese searches for Turbo parameter counts, 7B lineage and newer disclosures found no stronger primary specification superseding the dated launch relationship.

sources.title: Qwen2.5-7B official language-model configuration
sources.evidence: Read the small base-model config and compared it with the Omni Thinker text_config. They match on hidden size 3584, intermediate size 18944, 28 layers, 28 attention heads, 4 KV heads, 152064-token vocabulary and untied embeddings. The original Omni report explicitly says its LLM component is initialized from Qwen2.5. Together these primary sources support scoping the inherited nominal 7B designation to the Thinker language decoder, excluding modality encoders, Talker and token2wav; no complete-system tensor count is inferred.

sources.title: Qwen3 Technical Report, Qwen2.5-7B nominal activated count
sources.evidence: Parent reopened October 27, 2026. Table 6 lists Qwen2.5-7B Base and Table 18 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as 7B activated. Omni report section 3 initializes its LLM from Qwen2.5, and the existing exact text-config comparison identifies the 7B decoder. This supports an inherited nominal 7B active Thinker decoder, not full multimodal service activity.

name.note: Human-readable normalization of the documented qwen-omni-turbo identifier.

developer.note: Official repository API example identifies Qwen Team, Alibaba Group.

family.note: The official Qwen project provides this endpoint as its Omni API service.

release_date.note: Earliest explicitly listed release of this undated API ID is Beijing, February 14. Baseline January 19 is a snapshot date, not the documented release of this alias. International launch followed July 18.

open_weights.note: The immutable Qwen2.5-Omni launch announcement offers the named Omni-7B model on Hugging Face and DashScope. The launch README identifies qwen-omni-turbo as API access to that model; retained official documentation maps the alias to its March 26 snapshot. The official Omni-7B repository contains public downloadable weights. Classified open by this named-model mapping; API voice choices and serving features do not establish byte-identical deployed tensors.

license.note: No exact-endpoint weight license established; licenses of separate downloadable Qwen2.5-Omni checkpoints are not transferred to the service.

parameters_b.note: Inherited nominal 7B Thinker language decoder. The March 26 announcement identifies Qwen2.5-Omni-7B and makes the model available on DashScope; the same-day official README identifies qwen-omni-turbo as its API access. The report names a Qwen2.5-initialized LLM component, and the official Omni Thinker text configuration matches Qwen2.5-7B on all principal parameter dimensions. This supports the proposed thinker_decoder scope; 7B excludes modality encoders, Talker and token2wav and is not a complete multimodal total. No structural change defeating this nominal lineage inference was found.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 7B active scoped only to thinker_decoder, inferred through explicit Qwen2.5 initialization and matching 7B text parameter dimensions. Qwen3 report Tables 6/18 explicitly publish 7B activated for the Qwen2.5-7B base/instruct. Launch announcement and API example identify Turbo with Omni. Modality encoders, Talker and speech decoder are excluded; a complete multimodal active count remains unspecified.

architecture.note: Dense Thinker-Talker model architecture inherited through the same explicit launch-model relationship used for nominal size. The official 7B configuration uses ordinary dense feed-forward transformer blocks and modality encoders, without routed experts. This is a lineage-based specification, not a claim of identical deployed tensors.

context_window.note: Documented total context; input/output limits are 30,720/2,048 tokens.

modalities.note: Inputs: text, image, audio, video. Outputs: text, audio.

reasoning.note: Official indexed pricing labels this endpoint Non-Thinking. This means no dedicated thinking mode, not absence of general reasoning ability. Fresh page has removed the legacy row.

tool_call.note: Function Calling is explicitly unsupported; baseline true is contradicted.

description.value: Hosted Qwen multimodal model accepting text, images, audio, and video and generating streamed text and speech.
description.note: Replaces unsupported agent-task framing with documented input/output behavior.

patch.notes: Nominal 7B total and active cover the Thinker language decoder, inferred from the Qwen2.5-Omni-7B launch, Turbo API example, matching Qwen2.5-7B text configuration and the base’s published activated count. Full multimodal total and active counts remain unspecified. Dense Thinker-Talker architecture is inherited from the named model; the alias maps to the March 26, 2025 snapshot. Open weights through the developer's explicit mapping to downloadable Qwen2.5-Omni-7B. API voice choices and serving features may differ from local inference.

summary: Resolved weight availability. The immutable Qwen2.5-Omni launch announcement offers the named Omni-7B model on Hugging Face and DashScope. The launch README identifies qwen-omni-turbo as API access to that model; retained official documentation maps the alias to its March 26 snapshot. The official Omni-7B repository contains public downloadable weights. Classified open by this named-model mapping; API voice choices and serving features do not establish byte-identical deployed tensors. All unrelated field assessments and previous parameter/date evidence are preserved.

availability_resolution.rule: Publicly downloadable model weights or explicitly identified equivalent checkpoint => open. No such release found after original documentation and developer inventory checks => closed. API serving extras and weight licenses are separate.
limitations: The classification uses the developer's named-model mapping and the retained March 26 alias mapping; it does not claim byte-identical deployed tensors or identical API and local serving features.
